html:
The Chuj are a Maya people of the highlands of northwest Guatemala, in the department of Huehuetenango, and of the border area of Chiapas in Mexico, where the map places this land. They speak a Mayan language close to Q'anjob'al and Popti'.

They farmed maize on steep mountain slopes and traded salt from the springs of San Mateo Ixtatán, a town with old Maya ruins. The Spanish took the area in the 1520s and 1530s, but it stayed remote and the Chuj often rose against priests and officials. During Guatemala's civil war in the early 1980s, the army massacred Chuj villages, and thousands fled across the border to Chiapas, where some settled for good. Their earlier history belongs to the world of the Maya.
